title: [HELP/FEATURE] Add support to NuttX RTOS
body:
Hi @leleliu008 I just found your ppkg thanks to this post: https://www.reddit.com/r/linux/comments/1049jjw/ppkg_a_standalone_package_manager_that_doesnt/ while searching for an alternative to opkg.

We want to add support to package management on (Apache) NuttX RTOS to create a NuttX Distro. If you never heard about NuttX before, it is a RTOS used on PX4 flight controller drones, used on kernel of Xioami HyperOS Vela ecosystem (more thank 1000 SKUs products from there are using it, including Mi Band 9, 10, etc).

We created an Issue on NuttX project to discuss about the distro creation: https://github.com/apache/nuttx/issues/17351

Please feel free to jump in the discussion, we will love hear from you!

title: consider caching source files to a fixed server
body:
> _This may not be entirely related_
> 
> I know ppkg is not stable yet & you don't want to set up a prebuilt cache right now.
> But what about just the source cache?
> 
> My recommendation would be [huggingface hub datasets](https://huggingface.co/docs/datasets/en/index) (They are like git repos & can store anything as LFS). For public, it is unlimited storage.
> https://huggingface.co/docs/huggingface_hub/en/guides/upload
> 
> Similarly, ghcr is another great alternative with very large limit for per package container.
> https://oras.land/docs/
> 
> [Stal/ix](https://github.com/stal-ix/ix) uses both huggingface & ghcr as cache: https://github.com/stal-ix/ix/blob/main/pkgs/die/scripts/mirrors.txt
> Currently, it distributes only source tars
> So, you could use https://github.com/leleliu008/ppkg-formula-repository-official-core/blob/master/.github/workflows/check-if-alive.yml to fetch all the sources and then upload them to huggingface & ghcr
> 
> This will prevent network related errors like https://github.com/leleliu008/ppkg-formula-repository-official-core/issues/106
> 
>  

 _Originally posted by @Azathothas in [#15](https://github.com/leleliu008/ppkg/issues/15#issuecomment-3077366709)_

title: [Q] Is the C version abandoned?
body:
Hi, its been some time. I would like to know if the C version of `ppkg` is still being worked on, partly because I find `ppkg` source to be too long and difficult to read. The project has many dependencies and is written in shell, which is not ideal for software so complex, if the C version has been abandoned, but the desire for a rewrite hasn't, perhaps using Go or C++ would be better, as these languages offer good abstractions that make the codebase less complex, as it needs to implement less common stuff and can focus on the actual logic of `ppkg`

thanks by the way for the efforts, ppkg is impressive software, it benefits @pkgforge and inherently [dbin](github.com/xplshn/dbin) a lot

title: consider checking whether the generated executables are really fully statically linked when --static option is given
body:
Thanks!

Also, if I may ask, 
can a failsafe be added to prevent a situation like this in the future?

Example, `--static` was passed, then check that all executables are static, if they aren't fail the build
I see you already have https://github.com/leleliu008/ppkg/blob/master/core/check-if-has-dynamic-section.c
Adding this failsafe in ppkg would be highly highly useful.

I want my build to fail if it can't be statically linked.
As it is better than build to be successful but the executable to be dynamic
And if build fails, I can immediately know about it and then raise the issue to you.
But currently, some user has to manually download & run it only to find that it's not at all static

_Originally posted by @Azathothas in https://github.com/leleliu008/ppkg-formula-repository-official-core/discussions/11#discussioncomment-12283381_

title: consider providing `--head` option to fetch source code from `git HEAD`
body:
Is there a simple way to automatically force update a formula to build from git-src/latest commit?

There's a lot of packages that are very out of date.
And in some cases, upstream makes new commits which fixes bugs etc but they don't publish release.

I wanted to ask if there was a way, at least for formula using github, where we can force it to build from latest git.
This will ofc exclude formulae that need patches or fixes, but should work for others.

title: [+] `--profile="release"` should use `-Wl,--build-id=none` linker flag to avoid embedding `BuildID[sha*]`
body:
Hi, this is a minor nitpick, but `--profile="release"` should also strip `BuildID` from final executables.
Building a lot of binaries and doing `file $BINARY` spams the logs.
No worries if this doesn't get added, this is just personal preference, and it might actually be helpful for people to have the `BuilID` in their binaries for easy identification.
